original_recipe.mass_definition: Terminal product inventory P[g/L]*V[L]/1000. No harvest occurs before96h; stopped batches count zero produced/released product.

evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: ~10.02 mg/L at 48.0 h → 2.99 at 48.2 h → 1.80 mg/L at 52.0 h, crossing the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Delayed assay: P = 0.98 g/L (36h), 2.82 g/L (48h); source batches reached ~8 g/L by 72h — growth ongoing, high OUR

Forward model (source-calibrated, nominal): transfer multiplier 0.438; strong_feed_reduction min DO 1.16 mg/L, deficit 3.88 mg·h/L, 172.6 kg product — best among keep/reduce_feed/increase_air/combined
All four non-stop actions infeasible per nominal model; strong_feed_reduction has smallest oxygen-deficit integral and retains product mass
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed below the 2.0 mg/L minimum at ~48.2 h and sits at ~1.8 mg/L at the 52 h decision time, driven by impaired oxygen transfer (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.44). Aeration-only and mild feed cuts cannot close the deficit (model min DO 0.87–0.99, below-limit 9–11 h). A strong feed reduction to 0.6× cuts oxygen uptake enough to minimize the oxygen-constraint violation (min DO ~1.16, deficit integral ~3.9 vs 8.3 for aeration-only) while actually retaining the highest predicted product mass (~172.6 kg vs ~171.3–171.5 kg for milder actions, due to less dilution) and keeping the batch running to 96 h instead of stopping (zero counted production). This is the best bounded intervention available given the constraint cannot be fully satisfied.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect: all five sensitivity members remain infeasible, so the true receiving process may differ (better or worse). The DO2 deficit magnitude and the 0.44 transfer multiplier are estimates; if receiving transfer capacity is better than modeled, strong feed reduction is a conservative, product-preserving choice; if worse, no bounded action avoids constraint violation and a stop/abort decision would need escalation. Assay delay (4 h) means action must be taken on online sensor data.

evidence: Receiving DO2 collapse: 10.02 mg/L at 48.0h -> 2.99 mg/L at 48.2h, persisting at 1.80-2.99 mg/L through 52h (multiple readings below the 2.0 mg/L minimum)
Receiving P=2.82 g/L at 48h vs source batches 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L at the same age, indicating oxygen-limited production
All three source batches maintained DO2 >= ~7.4 mg/L, isolating the deficit to the receiving process aeration
bounded action range increase_air=[1.0, 1.15]
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~48 h from ~10 mg/L to the 2.0 mg/L constraint floor (readings as low as 1.80 mg/L), while product P (2.82 g/L at 48 h) is already behind all three source batches (3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L). This is a receiving-specific aeration deficit, not a source characteristic. Increasing air (bounded 1.15x) directly restores DO above the minimum constraint while leaving feed unchanged, preserving substrate for continued product formation and retaining product mass. Keep is unsafe (constraint violation continues); feed reductions would further suppress already-lagging production; stop gives zero production.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters are unavailable, so I cannot confirm that a 1.15x air increase fully clears the DO deficit; DO must be rechecked after implementation. Feed limitation is not completely ruled out as a co-factor, but the timing of the drop (abrupt at ~48 h, not gradual) and the DO trajectory argue for an aeration event.
